Trustworthy Evaluation of AI-Assisted Painting Restoration

HINT

Evaluation status: fully_evaluated. This report summarizes validated Notebook 09–30 evidence and creates no new scientific evidence.

Executive Summary

This standalone report evaluates HINT using validated restoration, metric, robustness, uncertainty, failure, explanation, and compute evidence.

What the evidence shows

  • Evaluation status: fully_evaluated.
  • Coverage: 300 paintings, 2620 cases and 2620 candidates.
Conclusion: HINT ranked second among the four full-scope methods. It performed better than some comparators and worse than others.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

1. Method Identity

This section defines what the evaluated method is, what role it can reasonably serve, and where that role ends.

Field Value
Model family Learned Mask Aware Transformer Inpainting
Methodological role Learned Deterministic Mask Aware Transformer
Implementation Official HINT generator loaded directly
Model identifier hint_places2_official
Deterministic True
Prompt dependent False
Execution device cuda
Precision float32

Intended uses

  • deterministic structure-aware learned inpainting comparison
  • controlled digital restoration candidate generation
  • full-scope comparison with classical, convolutional and diffusion methods

Excluded uses

  • historically verified reconstruction
  • artist authentication or conservation approval
  • calibrated uncertainty estimation
Thesis alignment: RQ3: establishes the method's role inside a human-centred workflow.

What the evidence shows

  • Methodological role: learned deterministic mask aware transformer.
  • Strengths: deterministic learned transformer family distinct from LaMa; native 768 x 768 execution under the validated adapter; full controlled-300 coverage.
  • Weaknesses: general-scene rather than painting-specific training; no prompt or repeated-seed uncertainty mechanism; plausible structure may remain historically unsupported.
Conclusion: HINT should be interpreted within its declared methodological role rather than as an autonomous restoration authority.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

3. Overall Quality Evidence

Eleven transparent quality anchors combine classical, perceptual, feature, spatial, local, semantic, and structural evidence. Lower plotted rank is better.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: compares restoration quality using complementary evidence.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place transparent quality anchors: 0 of 11.
  • Family-balanced baseline rank: 2 of four full-scope methods.
Conclusion: HINT ranked second among the four full-scope methods. It performed better than some comparators and worse than others.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

4. Damage Types and Experiments

This section keeps damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, and synthetic-degradation evidence separate. Positive adverse slopes indicate worse restoration behaviour under the stated exposure.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: evaluates damage size, mask geometry and synthetic degradation.

What the evidence shows

  • Damage-size deterioration was supported on 10 of 11 anchors.
  • 1 of 11 intervals crossed zero and remain inconclusive.
  • The focused damage-size, mask and degradation cohorts contain 35 paintings balanced across the five visual categories.
Conclusion: Larger damage made HINT worse on 10 anchors whose intervals remained above zero. Other anchors remain inconclusive.
Limitation: Focused experiments use controlled 35-painting cohorts. Metric-native slope magnitudes are not directly interchangeable.

5. Texture, Colour, and Seam Behaviour

Local texture, colour, and seam diagnostics test whether a plausible-looking repair remains visibly inconsistent near or inside the restored region.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: evaluates localized defects missed by global similarity.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place local anchors: 0 of three.
  • The anchors cover texture error, masked colour difference and boundary-seam mismatch.
Conclusion: HINT ranked first on 0 of the three local evidence anchors.
Limitation: Texture, colour and seam measurements represent different failure modes and use different scales.

6. Semantic and Structural Evidence

Semantic and structural measurements test local content and organization beyond pixel similarity. They remain proxies rather than proof of historical meaning.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and the semantic/XAI extension: evaluates local structure and feature agreement.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place semantic or structural anchors: 0 of three.
  • Evidence covers local DINO similarity, structural affinity and structural SSIM.
Conclusion: HINT ranked first on 0 of the three semantic and structural anchors.
Limitation: Feature agreement does not establish iconographic correctness, artist intent or historical truth.

7. Uncertainty, Prompt, and Stability Evidence

Uncertainty is treated as empirical repeated-seed variability only. Deterministic methods and insufficient seed coverage are reported as not applicable.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: distinguishes stochastic sensitivity from restoration quality.

What the evidence shows

  • HINT is deterministic under the evaluated configuration.
  • Repeated-seed diffusion uncertainty is therefore not applicable.
Conclusion: HINT is exactly repeatable under the recorded configuration. This does not imply better restoration quality.
Limitation: Empirical disagreement is not calibrated confidence and does not measure historical correctness.

9. Difference and Explanation Maps

These panels pair restored outputs with available difference, uncertainty, semantic, texture, colour, seam, or boundary diagnostics. Bright or intense regions must be interpreted using each map's stated scale.

Thesis alignment: RQ3: supports localized human review rather than opaque acceptance.

What the evidence shows

  • 14 diagnostic-map tiles are embedded.
  • Maps originate from validated spatial, local, uncertainty and semantic manifests where applicable.
Conclusion: Diagnostic maps localize where a restoration changed or failed more clearly than scalar measurements alone.
Limitation: Map colour and intensity remain specific to each diagnostic definition.

What the evidence shows

  • Observed mean runtime: 6.117 seconds per candidate.
  • Observed p95 runtime: 7.851 seconds.
  • Projected central 300-painting runtime: 4.41 hours.
Conclusion: HINT was slower than the fastest evaluated method. This is a compute disadvantage, not a quality conclusion.
Limitation: Observed timings describe one workstation. Projected values are not executed runtime measurements.

12. Decision Support

Strengths

  • deterministic learned transformer family distinct from LaMa
  • native 768 x 768 execution under the validated adapter
  • full controlled-300 coverage

Weaknesses

  • general-scene rather than painting-specific training
  • no prompt or repeated-seed uncertainty mechanism
  • plausible structure may remain historically unsupported
Thesis alignment: RQ3: translates evidence into bounded human-review support.

What the evidence shows

  • Intended uses: deterministic structure-aware learned inpainting comparison; controlled digital restoration candidate generation; full-scope comparison with classical, convolutional and diffusion methods.
  • Main strengths: deterministic learned transformer family distinct from LaMa; native 768 x 768 execution under the validated adapter; full controlled-300 coverage.
  • Main weaknesses: general-scene rather than painting-specific training; no prompt or repeated-seed uncertainty mechanism; plausible structure may remain historically unsupported.
Conclusion: HINT is best used within its declared role and with comparison against references, diagnostics, flags and human judgement.
Limitation: The report supports prioritization and inspection; it does not authorize physical conservation treatment.

13. Limitations

The limitations below are retained from the canonical model card and evidence contract.

  • Runtime and memory observations describe one recorded local workstation and software environment.
  • The controlled 300-painting values are executed observations; only the explicitly labelled 600-painting and full-design SDXL values are projections.
  • Projected storage covers notebook-owned output artifacts and excludes model caches, environments, Git history, and downstream metric outputs.
  • SDXL scheduled 35 bounded cases across 30 paintings; 24 completed, one timed out and ten were skipped under the declared budget, so it cannot support a full-scope ranking.
  • LaMa per-case runtime includes transparent allocation from IOPaint batch wall-clock measurements.
  • Quality-anchor wins are descriptive validated Notebook 21 evidence, not a universal quality or conservation score.
  • HINT was trained on Places2 rather than conservation-restoration paintings.
  • A plausible completion is not evidence of historical authenticity or conservation suitability.
  • The deterministic run measures one fixed checkpoint and configuration, not model-family uncertainty.
  • Eligible synthetic-degradation cases are supplementary masked-removal diagnostics.
  • Runtime measurements describe the recorded local hardware and are not universal benchmarks.
Thesis alignment: RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3: defines what the evaluation does and does not establish.

What the evidence shows

  • Excluded uses: historically verified reconstruction; artist authentication or conservation approval; calibrated uncertainty estimation.
  • 11 persisted limitations are retained from the model card.
Conclusion: The evidence identifies comparatively better and worse metric-defined behaviour. Historical authenticity and physical conservation suitability remain inconclusive.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.
